ukmt-hamilton-2019-h1.prompt: A number of couples met and each person shook hands with everyone else present, but not with themselves or their partners. There were $31\,000$ handshakes altogether. How many couples were there?

ukmt-hamilton-2019-h2.prompt: The diagram shows a pentagon $ABCDE$ in which all sides are equal in length and two adjacent interior angles are $90^\circ$ (those at $A$ and $B$). The point $X$ is the point of intersection of $AD$ and $BE$. Prove that $DX=BX$.
ukmt-hamilton-2019-h2.answer: $ABCE$ is a square and $CDE$ is equilateral; angle chasing gives $\angle XBD=\angle BDX=30^\circ$.

ukmt-hamilton-2019-h3.prompt: A $4\text{ cm}\times4\text{ cm}$ square is split into four rectangular regions using two line segments parallel to the sides (one vertical and one horizontal, each running from edge to edge). How many ways are there to do this so that each region has an area equal to an integer number of square centimetres?

ukmt-hamilton-2019-h4.prompt: Each of $A$ and $B$ is a four-digit palindromic integer, $C$ is a three-digit palindromic integer, and $A-B=C$. What are the possible values of $C$? [A palindromic integer reads the same forwards and backwards.]

ukmt-hamilton-2019-h5.prompt: The area of the right-angled triangle in the diagram is $60\text{ cm}^2$. The triangle touches the circle (the circle touches the two lines through the legs and the hypotenuse), and one side of the triangle (a leg) has length $15$ cm, as shown. What is the radius of the circle in cm?

ukmt-hamilton-2019-h6.prompt: Nine dots are arranged in the $2\times2$ square grid shown (three rows of three). The arrow points north. Harry and Victoria take it in turns to draw a unit line segment to join two dots in the grid. Harry is only allowed to draw an east-west line segment, and Victoria is only allowed to draw a north-south line segment. Harry goes first. A point is scored when a player draws a line segment that completes a $1\times1$ square on the grid. Can either player force a win, no matter how the other person plays? (Answer with the name of the player who can, or 'neither'.)
